method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.claims: Supports stopping suspected serious reaction exposure, congestion features of TACO and delayed haemolytic reaction warning pattern. Does not itself establish every local handling procedure.

items.assessment: Immediate reaction pathway is defensible; giving another unit because the first is cold is an implausible distractor.
issues: Immediate reaction pathway is defensible; giving another unit because the first is cold is an implausible distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace with a plausible measure such as administering a prescribed antipyretic before implementing the reaction procedure; explain why stopping exposure leads.

items.assessment: The congestion pattern supports TACO; a stable old bruise is unrelated filler.
issues: The congestion pattern supports TACO; a stable old bruise is unrelated filler.
proposedChanges: Replace the old bruise with a clinically meaningful competing reaction pattern, such as new fever/rigors without congestion. Keep the TACO-supporting rather than definitive-diagnosis wording.

items.assessment: Delayed reaction teaching is useful but every key is new/worsening and every wrong choice unchanged/improved, so clinical knowledge is unnecessary.
issues: Delayed reaction teaching is useful but every key is new/worsening and every wrong choice unchanged/improved, so clinical knowledge is unnecessary.
proposedChanges: Use plausible new but less concerning findings such as mild resolving insertion-site tenderness, and classify foundation unless a follow-up case requires interpretation.

items.assessment: Identity discrepancy resolution is sound and options represent plausible shortcut errors, but task is foundational safety recognition.
issues: Identity discrepancy resolution is sound and options represent plausible shortcut errors, but task is foundational safety recognition.
proposedChanges: Classify foundation, or add a genuine verification/documentation problem requiring application beyond one mismatched identifier.

items.assessment: Compatible setup is appropriate; because both solutions are clear is a giveaway.
issues: Compatible setup is appropriate; because both solutions are clear is a giveaway.
proposedChanges: Use the plain choice of connecting through the existing dextrose line; leave appearance-not-compatibility explanation in rationale. Consider supplying a compatibility excerpt if application is intended.

items.assessment: Review of new baseline fever/chills is sensible; yesterday baseline and transfusion-treats-fever alternatives are implausible.
issues: Review of new baseline fever/chills is sensible; yesterday baseline and transfusion-treats-fever alternatives are implausible.
proposedChanges: Use credible competing actions such as obtaining ordered cultures, requesting routine premedication, repeating temperature, or reporting current symptoms before starting; specify what assessment is already completed if needed for one key.

items.assessment: Clinical bleeding and count are useful; only/alone/principal markers make distractors easy.
issues: Clinical bleeding and count are useful; only/alone/principal markers make distractors easy.
proposedChanges: Use comparable outcome clusters without limitation qualifiers, such as bleeding/count, haemoglobin/exertional tolerance, temperature/chills, and fluid balance/pressure; keep efficacy distinct from general safety monitoring.

items.assessment: The component-role explanation is correct but direct factual recall; solely fluid intake is weak.
issues: The component-role explanation is correct but direct factual recall; solely fluid intake is weak.
proposedChanges: Classify foundation and replace fluid-only rationale with a credible role confusion such as raising oxygen-carrying capacity.

items.assessment: Interruption glucose plan is valid; saline as nutrition and double-rate catchup are weak obvious errors.
issues: Interruption glucose plan is valid; saline as nutrition and double-rate catchup are weak obvious errors.
proposedChanges: Provide an interruption order/protocol and compare plausible rate/solution/glucose-monitoring responses; otherwise use focused interpretation of hypoglycaemia risk rather than generic call-plan against cartoon choices.

items.assessment: SATA monitoring domains are correct, but sole-appetite and stopping-all-labs alternatives are implausible.
issues: SATA monitoring domains are correct, but sole-appetite and stopping-all-labs alternatives are implausible.
proposedChanges: Use concrete monitoring proposals with realistic timing or clinical purpose, or a case with actual trends requiring selection rather than universal monitoring domains.

items.assessment: The central formulation and available peripheral access require route/formulation clarification; patency and slower infusion are credible misconceptions that do not establish venous suitability.
Dedicated access and compatibility checks are sound; clear-appearance proof and convenience-despite-access wording advertise errors.
issues: Dedicated access and compatibility checks are sound; clear-appearance proof and convenience-despite-access wording advertise errors.
proposedChanges: Present specific co-infusion or lumen-use choices directly and place the missing compatibility/manipulation reasoning in explanations.

items.assessment: Refeeding phosphate depletion is clinically useful, but calorie-alone and unrelated-because-IV wording make rejection trivial.
issues: Refeeding phosphate depletion is clinically useful, but calorie-alone and unrelated-because-IV wording make rejection trivial.
proposedChanges: Use parallel possible mechanisms or clinical interpretations: refeeding shift, renal retention, inadequate ongoing intake, or fluid dilution, with case data supporting the key.

items.assessment: Isotonic volume replacement role is correct, but this is direct solution-purpose recall and complete-nutrition/every-electrolyte alternatives are weak.
issues: Isotonic volume replacement role is correct, but this is direct solution-purpose recall and complete-nutrition/every-electrolyte alternatives are weak.
proposedChanges: Classify foundation; compare extracellular volume support, intracellular free-water replacement, oncotic pressure expansion, and glucose supply as parallel purposes.

items.assessment: Monitoring concentration/rate and sodium/neuro status is correct; thirst-rate adjustment and monitoring-can-stop are weak.
issues: Monitoring concentration/rate and sodium/neuro status is correct; thirst-rate adjustment and monitoring-can-stop are weak.
proposedChanges: Use a supplied correction protocol and actual trends to decide which findings require action, or compare concrete appropriate monitoring tasks with plausible timing errors.

items.assessment: New renal impairment should trigger potassium-plan review; faster-to-test-sooner is implausible and sole-adjustment cues the error.
issues: New renal impairment should trigger potassium-plan review; faster-to-test-sooner is implausible and sole-adjustment cues the error.
proposedChanges: Use plain plausible alternatives such as more dilute administration, obtaining a new potassium result, reviewing fluid balance, or clarifying the replacement order; distinguish the best action with current lab/ordered parameters.

items.assessment: The magnesium-toxicity pattern is correct; sedative and BP-alone alternatives are cartoon unsafe.
issues: The magnesium-toxicity pattern is correct; sedative and BP-alone alternatives are cartoon unsafe.
proposedChanges: Use relevant competing concerns or immediate actions such as reflex recheck, respiratory support, stopping exposure and notifying under protocol; make the first-action boundary clear without making every distractor unsafe.

items.assessment: The different drug purposes are correct, but fever contingency and interchangeable medicines are weak.
issues: The different drug purposes are correct, but fever contingency and interchangeable medicines are weak.
proposedChanges: Use parallel paired purposes, such as seizure prevention/BP control, fluid removal/BP control, uterine relaxation/seizure prevention, or reversed roles. Classify foundation.

items.assessment: Sampling contamination is a valuable interpretation, but ignore and assume wording creates two obvious errors.
issues: Sampling contamination is a valuable interpretation, but ignore and assume wording creates two obvious errors.
proposedChanges: Use competing concrete responses: protocol dose adjustment, redraw from an appropriate site, verify infusion programming, or repeat the same-lumen sample. Key must include safe interim protocol guidance rather than ignoring a possible true high result.

items.assessment: Excess block pattern is important; more analgesic, dressing-round delay and mobilization are implausible.
issues: Excess block pattern is important; more analgesic, dressing-round delay and mobilization are implausible.
proposedChanges: Compare high block with opioid sedation, vasovagal response or hypovolaemia using a sufficient clinical pattern, or use credible immediate protocol actions.

items.assessment: Early systemic local-anaesthetic toxicity is correct; continue-until-complete, solely-anxiety and confirms-numbness alternatives are too obvious.
issues: Early systemic local-anaesthetic toxicity is correct; continue-until-complete, solely-anxiety and confirms-numbness alternatives are too obvious.
proposedChanges: Give plausible competing clinical interpretations or preparatory actions. Retain stop-exposure and emergency readiness but remove giveaway qualifiers.

items.assessment: Occlusion of the open system is appropriate; checking a dressing date is irrelevant and before-assessing wording cues error.
issues: Occlusion of the open system is appropriate; checking a dressing date is irrelevant and before-assessing wording cues error.
proposedChanges: Use credible competing immediate actions such as obtaining oxygen, checking current vital signs, sealing the connection, and contacting the team; specify the first physical action to make occlusion uniquely best.

items.assessment: Prescribed flush volume/rate resolves residual drug without a bolus; disconnecting an empty bag and faster completion are recognizable delivery errors.
Blood-bank return process is sound; family-held cooling is implausible.
issues: Blood-bank return process is sound; family-held cooling is implausible.
proposedChanges: Replace family cooling with a plausible proposed storage choice such as an ordinary ice-filled cooler, and remove arbitrary next-round delay. Keep validated storage distinction explicit in explanation.

items.assessment: Avoiding rubbing is correct, but longer massage, same bruise and dose-by-bruise options are weak.
issues: Avoiding rubbing is correct, but longer massage, same bruise and dose-by-bruise options are weak.
proposedChanges: Use plausible postinjection technique alternatives (gentle pressure, brief massage, rubbing with alcohol, adhesive dressing pressure) and classify foundation; ensure only the stated product-supported technique is keyed.
